title: Contrast: although, even though, despite, however, nevertheless
grammarTitle: Contrast Markers — Showing the Other Side
grammarNote: Contrast markers (маркеры контраста) показывают, что два факта противоречат ожиданиям или контрастируют друг с другом. Разные contrast markers требуют разных грамматических структур. Выбор неправильного маркера или структуры — распространённая ошибка.

grammarTable.subject: although / even though
grammarTable.example: "Although it is expensive, it is worth it." / "Even though she studied, she failed."

grammarTable.subject: despite / in spite of
grammarTable.example: "Despite the cost, it is worth it." / "In spite of studying, she failed."

grammarTable.subject: however
grammarTable.example: "It is expensive. However, it is worth it." / "She studied; however, she failed."

grammarTable.subject: nevertheless
grammarTable.example: "The evidence is mixed. Nevertheless, the policy was approved."

grammarTable.subject: yet
grammarTable.example: "She worked hard, yet she failed." / "Small but powerful." / "Simple, yet effective."

grammarTable.subject: while / whereas
grammarTable.example: "While Kazakhstan is large, it has a small population." / "Kamila likes coffee, whereas Amir prefers tea."

grammarExtra.title: although / even though — followed by a clause

rows.example: "ALTHOUGH the cost is high, the benefits outweigh it." (acknowledges the cost, then contrasts)
"EVEN THOUGH she knew the risks, she continued." (stronger, more dramatic contrast)
"Although X, Y." OR "Y, although X." (flexible position)
✗ "Although the cost..." is wrong if "the cost" is the full noun phrase with no verb → use DESPITE.

grammarExtra.title: despite / in spite of — followed by noun or gerund

rows.example: "DESPITE the high cost, it is worth it." (noun: "the high cost")
"IN SPITE OF the cost, it is worth it." (same meaning as despite)
✗ "Despite she studied..." → ✅ "Despite studying..." or "Although she studied..."
"The cost is high. HOWEVER, the benefits are significant." (position: start of new sentence + comma)
"Evidence was mixed. NEVERTHELESS, the committee approved it." (stronger, more formal)
Cannot start main clause. "However" and "nevertheless" need a sentence/clause before them. ✅
"The cost is high; however, the benefits are significant." ✅ (semicolon before; comma after)
✅ "Despite WORKING hard" (gerund) OR "ALTHOUGH she worked hard" (clause).
✅ "Although the cost IS HIGH, it..." — "although" needs a full clause (verb required)!
✅ "HOWEVER, she studied..." — "however" starts a new sentence with a comma, not a clause.
✅ "DESPITE the cost" — NEVER "despite of." "In spite OF" ✅ but not "despite of".

grammarTip:
Contrast markers — правила структуры:

ALTHOUGH / EVEN THOUGH + clause (S + V):
"Although the cost is high, it is worth it." ✅
"Even though she studied, she failed." ✅

DESPITE / IN SPITE OF + noun / gerund:
"Despite the cost, it is worth it." ✅
"Despite studying hard, she failed." ✅
✗ НИКОГДА: "Despite she studied" → нужен noun/gerund!
✗ НИКОГДА: "Despite of" → только "In spite OF" ✅

HOWEVER / NEVERTHELESS — начало нового предложения:
"The cost is high. However, it is worth it." ✅
"The cost is high; however, it is worth it." ✅

WHILE / WHEREAS — параллельный контраст:
"While X, Y." / "Kamila likes tea, whereas Amir prefers coffee." ✅

exercises.text: ___ the price is high, the quality is excellent.
exercises.hint: "Although" + full clause (the price IS high). ✅ "Despite" needs a noun/gerund, not a clause.

exercises.text: ___ the high price, the quality is excellent.
exercises.hint: "Despite" + noun (the high price). ✅ "Although" needs a full clause with a verb.

exercises.text: "___ studying for three weeks, she didn't pass." (no subject in the clause)
exercises.hint: "Despite STUDYING for three weeks" — gerund (no separate subject). ✅ "Although" needs: Although SHE STUDIED (subject + verb).

exercises.text: "The food was expensive. ___, it was delicious."
exercises.hint: "HOWEVER," starts a new sentence with a comma. ✅ "However, it was delicious." — new sentence after a period or semicolon.

exercises.text: "Despite of the difficulties, she succeeded." is correct.
exercises.hint: ✅ "DESPITE the difficulties" — NEVER "despite of." "In spite OF" ✅ but "despite" has NO "of." ✅

exercises.text: "___ she knew the risks, she accepted the challenge." (clause with subject)
exercises.hint: "Although SHE KNEW the risks..." — full clause (subject + verb) → "although." ✅
"WHEREAS" is used to contrast two parallel things or people. "Amir... WHEREAS Kamila..." ✅ "While" also works here!

exercises.text: "The evidence was unclear. ___, the decision was made."
exercises.hint: "HOWEVER" ✅ and "NEVERTHELESS" ✅ — both work here. "Nevertheless" is slightly stronger/more formal.
"DESPITE + gerund (working hard)" ✅ is correct. "Although" needs a full clause with a subject. ✅

exercises.text: "Kazakhstan is vast. ___, its population is small."
exercises.hint: Two separate sentences → "HOWEVER," starts the second. "Kazakhstan is vast. HOWEVER, its population is small." ✅

exercises.text: "___ ___ the bad weather, the match continued." (preposition + "the")
exercises.hint: "In spite OF the bad weather." ✅ "In spite of" = same as "despite" but uses "of." "Despite THE bad weather" = also correct (no "of"). ✅

exercises.text: "She failed the exam ___ she had studied every day for a month."
exercises.hint: "She failed... ALTHOUGH she had studied every day." ✅ — "although" introduces a full clause (she had studied). "Despite" would need a noun/gerund.

questions.hint: "although" + FULL CLAUSE. "Although THE COST IS HIGH..." ✅ (not just a noun).
"despite" + NOUN or GERUND. "Despite THE HIGH COST" / "Despite WORKING hard." ✅

questions.text: "Despite of the cost" — What is wrong?
questions.hint: ✅ "DESPITE the cost." NEVER "despite OF." "In spite OF" ✅ but not "despite of."

questions.text: "___ the difficulty of the task, she completed it." (without a clause)
questions.hint: "DESPITE the difficulty..." — noun phrase (no verb) → "despite" or "in spite of." ✅

opts: At the start of a new sentence or after a semicolon
In the middle of a clause only
questions.correct: At the start of a new sentence or after a semicolon
questions.hint: "HOWEVER," starts a new sentence (after period or semicolon). "The cost is high. HOWEVER, it is worth it." ✅
"Even though" is more emphatic than "although" — it emphasises that the contrast is surprising or notable. ✅

questions.text: "She studied hard. ___, she failed the exam." (strong contrast)
questions.hint: "NEVERTHELESS" = despite what came before; strong formal contrast. ✅

questions.text: "___ Kamila likes cities, Amir prefers the countryside." (parallel contrast)
questions.hint: "WHILE" = parallel contrast between two things. "While X, Y." "Whereas" also works. ✅

questions.text: "In spite of" has the same meaning as:
questions.hint: "In spite OF" = "despite." Same meaning, both signal contrast, but "despite" has no "of." ✅

questions.text: "The exam was hard. ___ the difficulty, she passed."
questions.hint: "DESPITE the difficulty" — noun phrase (no verb) after "despite." ✅ "Although" needs a full clause.

questions.text: "___ it was expensive, the government purchased it." (start of sentence)
questions.hint: "ALTHOUGH/EVEN THOUGH it was expensive..." — full clause (it WAS expensive, subject + verb). ✅

questions.text: "The results were inconclusive; ___, the study was published." (between clauses)
questions.hint: After semicolon + contrast → "NEVERTHELESS," or "however,". "...inconclusive; NEVERTHELESS, the study was published." ✅
"YET" can join two clauses like "but": "She worked hard, YET she failed." ✅ (same meaning as "but" with slightly literary feel)

questions.text: Which is the most formal contrast marker?
questions.hint: "NEVERTHELESS" is the most formal. "However" is formal. "Yet" and "but" are informal/neutral. ✅

opts: "Although the cost, it is worth it."
questions.hint: "HOWEVER, the results were surprising." ✅ — "however" + comma at start of new sentence. ✅
